# Genuine criticality does not give residual Jensen on a primitive line in Z^2
n=1 local theorem in
`candidate 23a10e01167cf706`
to a primitive line in a higher-dimensional integer base. It is NOT
an OC counterexample. It has an actual globally deepest point, actual
critical ambient caps with own-fiber fraction exactly gamma_d, affine
whole-fiber volume roots, a complete integer base, and even the strict
no-heavy condition `max fiber volume < total/2^n` with n=2.

The construction was proposed by root; this note independently checks
all sections, all ambient halfspaces, the depth maximum, the exact
constants, and the previously proved paired-tail input.

## 1. The ordinary input and dependency scope

We use ordinary Grünbaum at a volume centroid and the proved paired
centroid-tail theorem:

    |T intersect {u.x>=t}|+|T intersect {u.x>=-t}|
       >=2 gamma_d |T|,                              (1)

for every centroid-zero d-dimensional convex body T, every nonzero
continuous normal u, and every real t. Closed boundary traces have
zero d-volume. The all-dimensional proof is in
`candidate 732b11a769399016`; its full
independent audit is
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

Both files were read for this certificate. The proof of (1) uses the
one-constraint Fradelizi--Guédon localization theorem with measure
concavity parameter 1/d<=1/2, not a two-constraint localization or an
unproved mixed-integer inequality. It reduces to centered affine-power
interval laws and proves their bounds by exact d=2,3 calculations
and the stated quadrature inequality in d>=4. That is the only
additional nonstandard auxiliary theorem used here. Its scalar
certificate verifier is also rerun with this certificate's checks.

## 2. Parameters and an actual full-dimensional body

Fix any integer d>=2. Write

    gamma=(d/(d+1))^d,        kappa=(1-gamma)^(1/d).

Choose b and an integer N>=1 satisfying

    2 kappa < b < 2,       a=2-b,
    2N+1 > 3 b^d.                                    (2)

These choices exist in every dimension. For a completely rational
choice one may take

    a=1/(2d),       b=2-1/(2d),       N=3*2^(d-1).

Indeed gamma>1/3, by the elementary binomial estimate proved in the
n=1 source, and Bernoulli's inequality gives

    (b/2)^d=(1-1/(4d))^d>=3/4>2/3>1-gamma.

Thus b>2 kappa. Also b<2 and `2N+1=3*2^d+1>3b^d`.

Let T be any centroid-zero d-simplex of volume one. It may have
rational vertices: translate the centroid of
`conv(0,e_1,...,e_(d-1),d! e_d)` to zero. Its volume is one.
Write its canonical barycentric functions as

    lambda_i(x)=1/(d+1)+ell_i(x),    i=1,...,d+1.

Then `sum_i ell_i=0`, and on T the range of each ell_i is
`[-1/(d+1),d/(d+1)]`.

In the integer base plane let

    P=conv{(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-N),(0,N)}
      ={z: |z_1|+|z_2|/N<=1},
    r(z)=1+(b-1)z_1.

Define the actual body

    C={(z,x): z in P, x in r(z)T} subset R^2 x R^d.   (3)

The scale r is positive on P, lying between a and b. The set C is
compact and convex: if `x=r(z)t` and `x'=r(z')t'`, their convex
combination belongs to `r((1-s)z+sz')T` because r is affine and
the normalized combination of t,t' has positive weights summing
to one. It is full-dimensional; a point over an interior base and
an interior point of its positive fiber has an open neighborhood
in C. Equivalently, (3) is the convex hull of the four lifted
vertex fibers of P.

The integer base is exactly

    P intersect Z^2 = {(0,j): -N<=j<=N, j integer}
                       union {(-1,0),(1,0)}.         (4)

Indeed any integer z_1 is -1,0,or1. If it is +/-1, the diamond
inequality forces z_2=0; if it is zero, exactly the displayed
column remains. Therefore all integer fibers are precisely

    C_(0,j)=T,     C_(-1,0)=aT,     C_(1,0)=bT.      (5)

There are no missing intermediate integer fibers. Their d-volume
roots are affine on the entire projection, not just on the
horizontal primitive line. In particular

    (aT+bT)/2=T=C_(0,0).

## 3. Exact measure and strict no-heavy condition

All fibers in (5) have positive d-volume. Thus q=d and the intrinsic
measure in this example is exactly the mixed fiber sum. Its total is

    M=H_d(C intersect (Z^2 x R^d))=2N+1+a^d+b^d.      (6)

For d>=2, gamma<1/2, so kappa>d/(d+1)>1/2. Consequently b>1 and
0<a<1, making b^d the largest fiber volume. Equation (2) gives

    M>4 b^d+a^d>4 b^d,
    max_z |C_z|=b^d<M/4.                            (7)

Thus this example even excludes a fiber carrying the fraction 2^-n
of the total for n=2. No zero-volume boundary fiber is removed.

## 4. A lower bound for every closed ambient halfspace at one actual point

Let y=((0,0),0). It belongs to the central fiber T. We prove that
every closed ambient halfspace containing it has mass at least

    Q=(2N+1)gamma+a^d.                               (8)

Translate a containing boundary parallel to itself until it passes
through y. It suffices to bound the resulting smaller closed
halfspace, written as

    H={alpha_1 z_1+alpha_2 z_2+u.x>=0}.

First suppose u!=0. The own fiber T contributes at least gamma by
ordinary Grünbaum. Each pair of column fibers at `(0,j),(0,-j)`,
1<=j<=N, has thresholds `-j alpha_2,+j alpha_2` in the same continuous
direction u. Equation (1) gives at least 2 gamma from each pair.

The remaining endpoint pair contributes at least a^d. Here is a
direct geometric proof retaining the actual common threshold. The
simplex satisfies `-T subset dT`: if x is in T, then

    lambda_i(-x/d)=(1-lambda_i(x))/d>=0

for every i. Also b>2 kappa>2d/(d+1), hence
`b>d(2-b)=da`, and therefore `-aT subset bT`. The endpoint traces
have thresholds alpha_1 on aT and -alpha_1 on bT. Consequently

    |aT intersect {u.x>=alpha_1}|
      +|bT intersect {u.x>=-alpha_1}|
    >= |aT intersect {u.x>=alpha_1}|
      +|-aT intersect {u.x>=-alpha_1}|
     = a^d.

The last equality uses reflection and the null common continuous
hyperplane boundary. It holds in proper, full, empty, and tangent
cases. Adding the disjoint fiber contributions proves (8).

If u=0, the source fiber lies on the closed boundary and is included
in full. Every opposite column pair includes at least one full T,
and includes both if alpha_2=0. Its mass is at least 1>=2 gamma.
The endpoint pair includes at least one full endpoint and hence
has mass at least a^d, including both when alpha_1=0. Since
1>=gamma for the own fiber, (8) follows again. This explicitly
retains all boundary mass of purely integer halfspaces.

Thus the lower bound is for EVERY closed ambient containing
halfspace, including those whose normals couple both integer
coordinates to all continuous coordinates.

## 5. Actual critical caps and the global maximum

For each canonical direction define

    H_i={ell_i(x)-2z_1>=0},       i=1,...,d+1.        (9)

Because b<2 and `d/(d+1)<1`, these caps strictly exclude bT at
`z=(1,0)`: its largest margin is `b*d/(d+1)-2<0`.
They strictly contain aT at `z=(-1,0)`, since its smallest margin
is `2-a/(d+1)>0`. On every column fiber, their trace is a canonical
centroid vertex cap of T, of exact volume gamma. Hence

    mu(H_i)=Q

for every i. They contain y on their boundaries, so the lower bound
of Section 4 is attained: y has raw depth Q, and every H_i is
genuinely critical there. Its captured own-fiber fraction is exactly
gamma<=1/2.

To verify that y is globally deepest, first consider ANY point on
ANY column fiber. The sum of the continuous margins ell_i(x) is
zero, so at least one is nonnegative. Thus the caps (9) cover every
column fiber, and the point has depth at most Q. They also contain
the entire left endpoint fiber.

At either exposed endpoint base, one can isolate each canonical
own-fiber cap by the explicit ambient halfspace

    ell_i(x)+3(z_1-1)>=0       at the right endpoint,
    ell_i(x)+3(-z_1-1)>=0      at the left endpoint.  (10)

On the corresponding endpoint the trace is `ell_i(x)>=0`. At every
other integer fiber the additional term is at most -3, while the
largest possible ell_i(x) is less than 2, so the cap is empty
there. These isolating caps have masses gamma b^d and gamma a^d,
respectively, and each family covers its own fiber because the
ell_i sum to zero. By (2),

    gamma b^d < (2N+1)gamma < Q.

Every endpoint point consequently has depth strictly smaller than
Q. These cases exhaust (4). The exact global maximum raw depth is
therefore Q, attained at the actual point y, without any claim
about uniqueness of the maximizing point.

## 6. Strict failure along a primitive nearest-neighbor line

Take the primitive integer direction e_1=(1,0). For any critical
cap H_i in (9), its original residual volume roots at the three
consecutive bases are

    f_(-e_1)=0,       f_0=kappa,       f_(e_1)=b.     (11)

The left strict residual is EMPTY, since the whole left fiber is
strictly captured. The right cap is EMPTY and its residual is the
entire bT. The source cap has fraction gamma, giving its residual
root kappa. Condition (2) therefore gives the strict reverse of
the proposed nearest-neighbor Jensen comparison:

    f_0=kappa < b/2=(f_(-e_1)+f_(e_1))/2.             (12)

This failure occurs simultaneously for all d+1 canonical critical
caps. It uses the original caps and original residuals, not a
reassigned or optimized row. Full-body BM along the line is exact.

The n=1 proof cannot apply its step mass identity here. A tilt in
z_1 leaves the traces on ALL `2N+1` column fibers unchanged, not
just the source fiber. Their mass supplies the `(2N+1)gamma`
term in (8). In fact this construction already captures every
negative-z_1 integer fiber fully and misses every positive-z_1
integer fiber, so the failure persists even in that particularly
simple step geometry. The uncontrolled off-line column is enough.

## 7. A small completely rational numerical instance

For d=2 take

    a=2/5,       b=8/5,       N=4,
    T=conv{(-1/3,-2/3),(2/3,-2/3),(-1/3,4/3)}.

Then |T|=1, gamma=4/9, kappa=sqrt(5)/3, and
`b/2=4/5>sqrt(5)/3` because `144>125`. The condition
`2N+1>3b^2` is `9>192/25`, so all preceding conclusions apply.
The continuous canonical linear forms can be taken as

    ell_1=x,       ell_2=y/2,       ell_3=-x-y/2.

The exact totals are

    Q=104/25,       M=293/25,
    max fiber volume=64/25<293/100=M/4,
    max normalized depth=104/293.

The own capture fraction is 4/9 and the primitive-line residual
roots are `(0,sqrt(5)/3,8/5)`. All body vertices, projection
vertices, and cap coefficients are rational. The square root in
the root comparison has the exact squared certificate above.

The OC target for this instance is `(1/4)(4/9)=1/9`, and
`104/293>1/9`. More generally, the construction's depth ratio is
strictly above gamma/4: (2) immediately makes
`4Q-gamma M=3(2N+1)gamma+(4-gamma)a^d-gamma b^d` positive.
Thus none of these examples contradicts OC.

The companion verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_critical_primitive_line_long_diamond.py`. Its exact checks
audit parameters, rational polygon masses in the planar instance,
closed supporting statuses, and the displayed identities. The
run passed 4,451 exact rational checks. The paired-tail theorem's
separate scalar-certificate verifier was also rerun successfully.
The all-dimensional proof is the geometric argument above together
with the separately proved ordinary paired-tail theorem (1).
